mission.title: kubernetes: Restore a PVC from a VolumeSnapshot after data corruption
mission.description: An application reports `database disk image is malformed` after data corruption on its PVC. Restore the data by creating a new PVC from an existing VolumeSnapshot.

steps.title: List available snapshots
steps.description:
```bash
kubectl get volumesnapshot -n data
kubectl get volumesnapshotcontent
```

Pick one with READYTOUSE `true` taken before the corruption.

steps.title: Scale down the workload using the corrupted PVC
steps.description:
```bash
kubectl scale statefulset/db -n data --replicas=0
kubectl get pods -n data
```

steps.title: Create a new PVC from the snapshot
steps.description:
```bash
kubectl apply -f restore-pvc.yaml
```

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: db-data-restored
  namespace: data
spec:
  storageClassName: csi-standard
  dataSource:
    name: db-snap-20261016
    kind: VolumeSnapshot
    apiGroup: snapshot.storage.k8s.io
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 20Gi
```

Size must be >= the snapshot's restoreSize.

steps.title: Point the workload at the restored PVC
steps.description:
```bash
kubectl patch statefulset db -n data --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/volumes/0/persistentVolumeClaim/claimName","value":"db-data-restored"}]'
kubectl scale statefulset/db -n data --replicas=1
```

steps.title: Verify data and clean up
steps.description:
```bash
kubectl get pvc db-data-restored -n data
kubectl logs statefulset/db -n data --tail=20
kubectl delete pvc db-data -n data
```

Delete the corrupted PVC only after validating the restored data.

resolution.summary: The root cause is that the live volume contained corrupted blocks, so the application could not read its database. A VolumeSnapshot holds a point-in-time copy at the storage layer, and provisioning a new PVC with `dataSource` clones that copy, because the CSI driver creates the volume from the snapshot rather than from the damaged volume.

prerequisites.description: A running Kubernetes cluster with kubernetes available or the issue environment reproducible.
